problems.claim: Anchore Enterprise pricing: 'not public; quote via sales (AWS Marketplace listing is contract-based, no single list price)' (source: get.anchore.com/request-pricing)
problems.issue: The cited page could not be opened: get.anchore.com does not resolve from this session. Search results for Anchore's AWS Marketplace listing (prodview-ilkug4gdyavdq) show published dollar figures: a $34,500 line for Anchore Enterprise hosts and a $15,000 Essential Customer Success Plan. Round 1 read those lines as $19,500 and $15,000. Either way, prices are publicly listed on the Marketplace, so 'not public' is contradicted. Only the 'no single list price' part holds.

problems.claim: WTP: 'Generation itself is free (Syft, GitHub, Docker, Inspector); buyers pay only inside SCA/management bundles such as Snyk Enterprise or Anchore'
problems.issue: None of the three cited sources shows how buyers spend money, so 'buyers pay only inside bundles' is an inference, not something the sources support. AWS Inspector SBOM export requires Inspector, which is a paid scanning service; search found no AWS statement that export comes at no extra cost. Docker is free for only 1 Scout repo, and Pro, Team and Business are paid ($9-24/user/mo per docker.com/pricing). So generation is not free across the board. The GitHub, AWS docs and Snyk docs hosts did not resolve, so the cited pages were checked only through search snippets.

problems.claim: WTP: 'Mend Renovate Enterprise $25,000/yr for 100 devs (about $21/dev/month)' (source: AWS Marketplace prodview-yinerd2u4nhw4)
problems.issue: Search snippets of the listing show 'Mend Renovate Enterprise 100 CDs, $25,000.00'. The listing does not define the unit 'CDs', and no snippet confirms a 12-month term. Both '/yr' and 'per developer' are therefore unverified, and so is the derived ~$21/dev/month. The listing page itself (aws.amazon.com) did not resolve from this session.

problems.claim: WTP: 'IT buyers pay ... Okta suites that include Lifecycle Management (Essentials from $17/user/month)' (source: okta.com/pricing)
problems.issue: The $17/user/month Essentials price is confirmed. Whether Lifecycle Management is included is contested: Okta's editions and regional pricing pages list Lifecycle Management as an add-on or under the Identity Governance add-on, while Capterra and Orb say Essentials includes it. The same theme's paid_market_gaps also claims Okta customers must buy a $4/user/month Lifecycle Management add-on, which contradicts this WTP sentence. okta.com did not resolve from this session.

problems.claim: Amazon RDS Proxy pricing: 'usage-based, per vCPU-hour (or per ACU-hour for Aurora Serverless), region-dependent' (source: aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2025/09/amazon-rds-proxy-end-to-end-iam-authentication)
problems.issue: The cited source is the What's New announcement for end-to-end IAM authentication. It covers the feature and its availability for MySQL/PostgreSQL in all RDS Proxy Regions and says nothing about pricing. The per-vCPU-hour/ACU-hour pricing comes from the RDS Proxy pricing page, which this row lists as the vendor url but does not cite as its source.

problems.claim: WTP: 'Vendr reports a StrongDM median of ~$33k/yr across 58 purchases'
problems.issue: Vendr's StrongDM marketplace page, as returned by search, gives a median of $33,346/yr based on 66 purchases, not 58. The ~$71k average matches the buyer guide, which bases it on 45 deals. vendr.com could not be fetched directly to confirm which count is current.

problems.claim: WTP: 'Cribl's pricing and minimums are reviewed as unsuitable for small and medium companies' (source: peerspot.com cribl_vs_stellar-cyber-open-xdr)
problems.issue: The PeerSpot comparison, as surfaced by search, does not say this. Its Cribl reviewers call it cost-effective at enterprise scale (around 30 cents/GB, cost savings appealing to mid-level and large enterprises). One reviewer asks for more features for smaller firms. No reviewer text about minimums, or about pricing being unsuitable for SMBs, was found. The same sentence is also used as a paid_market_gap with the same citation.

problems.claim: Aembit pricing: 'free Starter tier; Teams from $20/workload/month and $20/agent/month; Enterprise custom quote' (source: aembit.io/faq)
problems.issue: The cited FAQ page could not be confirmed to carry these prices. A search for Aembit's official pages found tier limits but no dollar figures, and G2 says Aembit has not published pricing. The $20/workload and $20/agent figures appear only on third-party sites (rfp.wiki, SpotSaaS). Aembit's AWS Marketplace listing shows a 'Workloads' dimension at $200 on a 36-month contract, which does not match. The WTP evidence repeats the $20 figure with the same unverified citation.

problems.claim: Teleport Machine & Workload Identity pricing: 'not public (bundled in Enterprise Standard; extra MWIs priced per unit)' (source: goteleport.com/pricing/guide/)
problems.issue: Teleport's June 16, 2026 pricing guide counts 'each unique instance of tbot as a TPR as determined by hourly average'. It shows no separate per-unit MWI price. Theme 7's Teleport row, citing that same guide, says 'no separate per-MWI price', which contradicts this row. 'Bundled in Enterprise Standard' is supported: the guide lists MWI in the Standard bundle. The 'extra MWIs priced per unit' part is not.

problems.claim: WTP: 'Oasis (now Cyera Identity) $50k/12-month starter on AWS Marketplace' (source: prodview-blsgeikmunnxc)
problems.issue: Not supported. A search of the cited listing found pricing text describing recurring monthly usage fees billed through AWS, not a $50k 12-month contract. A different listing (prodview-wl52yxutluvma, 'Cyera Identity (Oasis) Starter Pack') shows a 12-month contract at $100,000. The same unsupported $50k figure appears in the paid_market_gaps text. aws.amazon.com did not resolve from this session for a direct check.

problems.claim: Anchore Enterprise pricing: 'not public; quote via sales' (source: AWS Marketplace prodview-ilkug4gdyavdq)
problems.issue: The cited listing itself publishes dollar amounts: search snippets show $34,500 for Anchore Enterprise hosts and a $15,000 Essential Customer Success Plan, with round 1 reading $19,500 and $15,000. Calling the pricing 'not public' while citing a public price list is contradictory. What the listing supports is 'separate dimensions, no single list price'.

problems.claim: Interlynk pricing: 'AWS Marketplace contracts by active developers: $18,000 (10), $36,000 (25), $60,000 (50), $100,000 (100)' (source: prodview-n6mc7symiq2rm)
problems.issue: Could not be verified. The listing page (aws.amazon.com) does not resolve from this session. Search snippets of the listing mention four developer tiers and contract-based pricing but show none of the dollar amounts. Treat the figures as unconfirmed until the live pricing tab is checked.

iTechGuides does list $159/month billed annually, and it discloses that vendors can pay for ranking positions. SourceForge and Slashdot list sbomify at £49/month, and G2 says no pricing has been provided. The figure rests on a single paid-placement aggregator, not the vendor's own pricing page, and other aggregators contradict it.

problems.claim: WTP: 'Funded SBOM/VEX vendors sell quote-based subscriptions ... Prices not public.'
problems.issue: The cited Manifest release supports only one three-year device-maker deal of undisclosed value, which is a single data point and not evidence of a quote-based market. 'Prices not public' conflicts with theme 11's own evidence for the same vendor set: Interlynk AWS Marketplace contract tiers, sbomify from $159/mo, and Anchore's Marketplace line items. The CRA dates (reporting from 11 Sept 2026, main obligations from 11 Dec 2027) are supported by the Commission news item and SonarSource.
